title: ESP Atlas Recipe
description: One board x one firmware, the atomic 'what runs on what'. First-class entity like `brand`: never indexed into the queryable parts table, never a /search or /wizard result. `chip_family` must equal the referenced board's `soc`. See SPEC-wizard.md.

board.description: id of the board (must exist in data/boards/**)

firmware.description: id of the firmware (must exist in data/firmware/)

chip_family.description: must equal the referenced board's soc

parts.description: A multi-part image (e.g. bootloader, partition table, boot_app0, app), each written at its OWN offset and never merged: a merged image fills the gaps between parts (where NVS usually lives) with 0xFF. Emitted in order as the generated manifest's parts[], each via the same-origin proxy as `&part=<index>` (esp_atlas_core.flash). Mutually exclusive with `bin_url`. Cite-or-omit per part, checked by esp_atlas_core.validate: a sources[] entry with field `flash.parts[<i>].url` whose url IS that part's url (the binary itself, same convention as `flash.bin_url`), and one with field `flash.parts[<i>].offset` pointing where the offset is stated.

offset.description: hex string, e.g. '0x10000' (never a bare decimal, which reads ambiguously)
